findings.title: No-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not exist
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments so the username step is not skipped on re-authentication when passkeys are on. The only new method is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel); nothing in this class or its parents defines a no-arg overload, and there is no static import. services will not compile, so the re-authentication fix cannot build or be tested. The call has to match a real method that reports whether conditional passkeys are enabled (a no-arg check, or pass context.getUser() only if that helper does not require a non-null user).

findings.title: Passkeys UI removed from the unidentified-user login form
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) is true only when user != null, and both authenticate() (line 115) and the error challenge() override (line 137) use it before webauthnAuth.fillContextForm. That call used to run when the user was not yet selected (webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled()), which is how conditional passkeys are rendered on the first username/password page. Moving it out of the else branch and requiring a non-null user inverts that: initial login and invalid-credential redisplay no longer get a WebAuthn challenge, RP ID, or conditional UI, because context.getUser() is still null until validateUser, which runs only after a successful password check. Discoverable-key auto-login and the passkey control on the combined form stop working; existing tests such as PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey and passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey still expect username webauthn autocomplete and //form[@id='webauth'] on that first page. Passkeys should be filled whenever webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled(), including when the user is null, and additionally when the user is already set for re-authentication.
